newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-POOR RELATIONS ATLETICO HAVE GRUDGE TO SETTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-POOR RELATIONS ATLETICO HAVE GRUDGE TO SETTLE.

text.p: Atletico Madrid fans could be forgiven for feeling they have a grudge to settle in Saturday's derby game in the Spanish capital.
Long treated as the poor relations of mighty neighbours Real, Atletico lost both last year's derby matches despite ending the season 17 points ahead of their arch-rivals.

Atletico's superb league and Cup double campaign contrasted with a miserable year for the six-times European champions who failed to qualify for continental competition for only the second time in their illustrious history.
It was an extraordinary turn-around after a season in which Real took a record 26th title while Atletico had looked close to slipping into the second division for the first time in nearly 60 years.
Atletico are now without a league win over Real since the 1991-92 season, and it's a situation they'd badly like to put right.

"They've got luck with them, let's see when it ends" says Atletico coach Radomir Antic, who has strongly criticsed the excessive media attention given to the 'old firm' of Barcelona and Real -- a team often called simply 'Madrid'.

Antic has also complained that his team rarely play in front of a full house, a problem perhaps reflecting the fact that Atletico draw support from a fairly narrow base in the poorer areas of southern Madrid.
By contrast Real have a nationwide following dating from their 1950s glory days, together with the backing of the wealthier sections of Madrid society.
The favourite team of dictator General Franco, Real have become synonymous with the intolerant centralism of the Spanish right.
The social differences are reflected in contrasting styles of play.
Traditionally Real play a possession game, seeking to dominate their opponents from start to finish, while Atletico look to absorb pressure and strike back on the counter-attack.
Despite the tactical differences, there have been many instances of players who have moved between the two sides, and Saturday's game is likely to see at least three of them in action.

Nor does the animosity between fans in the Spanish capital mean that the clubs are not on friendly terms, and Atletico played their first game of the season in Real's Santiago Bernabeu stadium after pitch problems at the Vicente Calderon.
Neverthless controversial Atletico owner Jesus Gil has been quick to remind Spanish fans how the honours were shared last season -- his club's most successful ever.
"On Wednesday we're going to Dortmund, but (Real) are going to bed," gloated Gil ahead of a week of European competition fixtures.
